questiontext.text:
The triangle \(ABC\) below has vertices \(A={@ntupleify(A)@}\), \(B={@ntupleify(B)@}\) and \(C={@ntupleify(C)@}\).

Using the construction tools provided, construct the circumcircle of triangle \(ABC\).

GeoGebra displays the coordinates of the points you construct. Read off the position of the circumcentre and the radius of the circumscribed circle (the circumradius), and enter them below, each rounded to 3 decimal places.

[[geogebra set="A__fixed,B__fixed,C__fixed" width="1200px" height="600px"]] params["material_id"]="dcdnc4ee"; /* Restricted compass-and-straightedge toolbar. customToolBar OVERRIDES the file's toolbar; numbers are GeoGebra tool IDs, | starts a new menu. 0 Move, 6 Delete | 5 Intersect | 2 Line | 10 Circle(centre,point) | 8 Perpendicular-bisector, 4 Perpendicular line | 38 Distance or Length. Provides 8 Perp-bisector (the natural tool for the circumcentre), 4 Perpendicular line, and 38 to measure the radius. */ /* params["appName"]="geometry"; */ params["showToolBar"]=true; params["customToolBar"]="0 | 6 | 5 | 2 | 10 | 9 | 4 | 8 | 38"; params["showToolBarHelp"]=false; /* Hide the algebra input bar and menu bar. NOTE: the algebra VIEW panel is governed by the saved file (perspective is ignored with material_id), so ALSO close the Algebra View in the GeoGebra material and re-save. */ params["showAlgebraInput"]=true; params["algebraInputPosition"]="bottom"; params["showMenuBar"]=false; params["showResetIcon"]=true; params["showFullscreenButton"]=true; [[/geogebra]]
Circumcentre \(O = (\,\) [[input:xc]] \(,\) [[input:yc]] \(\,)\) \( (\,\)[[validation:xc]], [[validation:yc]] \(\,)\)
[[feedback:prt1]]
Circumradius \(R = \) [[input:r]] [[validation:r]]
[[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The centre of the circumscribed circle is the circumcentre: the point where the three perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet. It is the unique point equidistant from all three vertices, so the distance from it to each vertex is the same — that common distance is the circumradius \(R\).

Construction. Construct the perpendicular bisector of any two sides (say \(AB\) and \(BC\)) using the perpendicular-bisector tool; their intersection \(O\) is the circumcentre. Drawing the circle centred at \(O\) through any vertex gives the circumscribed circle, and the distance from \(O\) to that vertex is the circumradius. (For an obtuse triangle \(O\) lies outside the triangle.)

[[geogebra set="A__fixed,B__fixed,C__fixed" width="1200px" height="600px"]] params["material_id"]="pcttvewn"; /* Restricted compass-and-straightedge toolbar. customToolBar OVERRIDES the file's toolbar; numbers are GeoGebra tool IDs, | starts a new menu. 0 Move, 6 Delete | 5 Intersect | 2 Line | 10 Circle(centre,point) | 8 Perpendicular-bisector, 4 Perpendicular line | 38 Distance or Length. Provides 8 Perp-bisector (the natural tool for the circumcentre), 4 Perpendicular line, and 38 to measure the radius. */ /* params["appName"]="geometry"; */ params["showToolBar"]=true; params["customToolBar"]="0 | 6 | 5 | 2 | 10 | 9 | 4 | 8 | 38"; params["showToolBarHelp"]=false; /* Hide the algebra input bar and menu bar. NOTE: the algebra VIEW panel is governed by the saved file (perspective is ignored with material_id), so ALSO close the Algebra View in the GeoGebra material and re-save. */ params["showAlgebraInput"]=true; params["algebraInputPosition"]="bottom"; params["showMenuBar"]=false; params["showResetIcon"]=true; params["showFullscreenButton"]=true; [[/geogebra]]

For this triangle the circumcentre is \(O \approx ({@dispdp(ta_O[1],3)@},\ {@dispdp(ta_O[2],3)@})\) and the circumradius is \(R \approx {@dispdp(ta_R,3)@}\).

node.description: Both circumcentre coordinates correct to 3 d.p.?

truefeedback.text: The centre is correctly placed at the circumcentre.

node.description: Did they find the orthocentre instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the orthocentre — where the three altitudes meet (each a perpendicular dropped from a vertex to the opposite side). For the circumcircle you need the perpendicular bisectors of the sides: lines perpendicular to a side through its midpoint, not through a vertex.

node.description: Did they find the incentre instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the incentre — where the three angle bisectors meet. It is equidistant from the three sides, not the three vertices. For the circumcircle you must perpendicularly bisect the sides, not bisect the angles.

node.description: Did they find the centroid instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the centroid — where the three medians meet (the triangle's balance point). The circumcircle's centre is equidistant from the vertices, which you get from the perpendicular bisectors of the sides.

falsefeedback.text: Your point \(O\) is not the circumcentre. The circumcentre is where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides cross — check that each line you drew is perpendicular to a side and passes through that side's midpoint.

node.description: Did they give the inradius instead of the circumradius?

truefeedback.text: That is the inradius — the radius of the inscribed circle (the one that fits inside the triangle, touching all three sides). Here you want the circumradius: the radius of the circle through the three vertices, which is the distance from the circumcentre \(O\) to any vertex.

falsefeedback.text: Your circumradius is not correct (to 3 decimal places). The circumradius is the distance from the circumcentre to any vertex — measure from \(O\) to \(A\), \(B\) or \(C\).

qtest.description: Correct: circumcentre and circumradius both correct
Neither a recognised centre nor circumradius
Centre correct but gave the inradius instead of the circumradius
